content.title: Planar Folktale Variant | Color Chapters and Object Relay
content.summary: Establish a flat original story world with one emblematic object that reveals the protagonist. Use a distinct background color and one object duty for each chapter. Carry one recognizable object across chapters to recruit or connect the ensemble. Compress travel and confrontation into readable silhouettes without changing the graphic grammar. Return the group and transformed object to a simple final emblem that proves resolution.

quick_start.input_format: Establish a flat original story world with one emblematic object that reveals the protagonist. + Use a distinct background color and one object duty for each chapter. + Carry one recognizable object across chapters to recruit or connect the ensemble. + Compress travel and confrontation into readable silhouettes without changing the graphic grammar. + Return the group and transformed object to a simple final emblem that proves resolution.
quick_start.recommended_input: On a flat ochre field, an original brass compass opens like a small book and reveals a clearly adult polar courier in a teal coat; keep simple paper-cut shapes. Shift through teal, violet and green chapters as the same route token recruits an adult radio engineer, an adult sled mechanic and an adult medic, one companion per beat. The beacon turns warm gold; return to ochre as all four adults stand beside the open compass, now displaying one complete illuminated route crest. Hold without extra text.

usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Establish a flat original story world with one emblematic object that reveals the protagonist. Use a distinct background color and one object duty for each chapter. Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.

not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Establish a flat original story world with one emblematic object that reveals the protagonist. Use a distinct background color and one object duty for each chapter. Carry one recognizable object across chapters to recruit or connect the ensemble. Compress travel and confrontation into readable silhouettes without changing the graphic grammar. Return the group and transformed object to a simple final emblem that proves resolution. The reusable mechanism is the ordered baseline, trigger, continuity, controlled escalation and terminal proof—not the source identities, brands, wording, locations, props, exact styling, choreography, camera path, creator identity or timing.

invariants.rule: Establish a flat original story world with one emblematic object that reveals the protagonist.
invariants.purpose: Makes the baseline measurable before the mechanism changes it.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without the baseline, later change has no trustworthy reference state.

invariants.rule: Use a distinct background color and one object duty for each chapter.
invariants.purpose: Binds the first visible change to a specific cause rather than decoration.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without a visible trigger, the transition reads as an arbitrary edit.

invariants.rule: Carry one recognizable object across chapters to recruit or connect the ensemble.
invariants.purpose: Preserves identity, material or spatial continuity through the middle transition.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without continuity, the sequence becomes unrelated montage or identity drift.

invariants.rule: Compress travel and confrontation into readable silhouettes without changing the graphic grammar.
invariants.purpose: Raises intensity or information while retaining the same readable grammar.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without controlled escalation, the middle either plateaus or turns into noise.

invariants.rule: Return the group and transformed object to a simple final emblem that proves resolution.
invariants.purpose: Provides a terminal proof that resolves the mechanism instead of merely stopping.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without terminal proof, the promised result or reversal remains unverified.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: source Momotaro characters, childlike proportions and costumes
source peach, dumplings, animals, island, oni and treasure cart
source Japanese wording, flag and folk symbols
source exact color chapters, actions, timing and layouts
source creator identity, MiniMax H3 claim, platform marks and prompt wording
